content: Ligand 1 is the oxadiazole-benzofuran from the start of this generation; atom 0 is its methoxy methyl over an acyclic bond, so the surviving carbon has to appear somewhere in the product and the natural place is on a C4 substituent that contains a methyl. A methylsulfonyl is the one I want. It is the most strongly electron-withdrawing group I can put there, bulky and tetrahedral rather than planar, and it carries two acceptor oxygens - so it is about as far from bromine as a substituent can be while still being roughly the same size. It also does something no other candidate does: it takes nearly two log units off lipophilicity. My best molecule sits at LogP 4.2, which is past where QED starts penalising, so if this group carries activity at all it should post a strong QED despite the extra 25 Da. Together with the methyl ketone it gives me two strongly withdrawing groups of quite different shape and polarity, which is what the scan needs to separate withdrawal from bulk. Expected product: about 331 Da at LogP near 2.3.
